jobs.description:
**Position Summary:**

Community Federal Savings Bank (CFSB), located in New York City, is seeking an FIU Analyst to join our Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) in the Compliance department. CFSB offers a full range of banking services, including ACH settlement services, pre-paid card issuance, and retail banking. In addition to serving our general customer base, we also service various types of money service businesses and FinTech companies.

This individual will be responsible for performing financial intelligence reviews involving potentially unusual or suspicious activity across the Bank’s products, customers, and partner programs. Under established procedures and appropriate guidance, the FIU Analyst will review alerts and referrals, analyze transactional activity and customer information, conduct relevant internal and external research, document findings, recommend appropriate dispositions, and escalate matters requiring further investigation or consideration. The FIU Analyst will contribute to timely, accurate, and consistent FIU reviews and documentation.

\*\*The role is fully remote in 24 select states or hybrid for those located in the NYC Metro area.

\*\*This position supports ongoing hiring needs and may remain posted on a continuous basis. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and candidates may be considered for current or future openings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Review assigned transaction monitoring alerts, internal or external referrals, and other FIU work items in accordance with established procedures and timelines.
* Review transactional activity, customer profiles, account history, prior investigations and filings, and relevant internal and external research to identify potential financial crime risk indicators and unusual patterns.
* Prepare clear, complete, and accurate review documentation and case narratives that summarize activity reviewed, research performed, findings, and rationale.
* Recommend alert or case dispositions based on available information and established guidance and promptly escalate potential suspicious activity or other matters requiring additional review.
* Manage assigned work items and priorities to meet review deadlines and quality expectations.
* Collaborate with FIU colleagues and seek guidance from experienced investigators or FIU leadership when questions or complex matters arise.
* Identify and communicate observed trends, recurring issues, and potential process concerns to FIU management.
* Develop knowledge of AML/BSA regulatory requirements, financial crime risks, enforcement trends, and relevant typologies through training and practical experience.
* Assist with special projects and other FIU priorities, as assigned.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**

* Ability and willingness to learn and apply AML/BSA requirements, financial crime concepts, suspicious activity monitoring processes, and SAR requirements through training and practical experience.
* Ability to review transactional and customer information, recognize relevant risk indicators or unusual patterns, and document findings clearly.
* Strong attention to detail, willingness to learn, and ability to manage a deadline-driven workload while following established procedures.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) or related software; familiarity with transaction monitoring or case management systems is a plus.
* Analytical, organizational, research, and problem-solving skills.
* Clear verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to summarize research and findings in a concise, organized manner.
* Ability to follow procedures, work collaboratively, manage assigned tasks, and seek guidance when needed.

**Education, Training, and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Criminal Justice, Risk Management, Compliance, or a related field; or equivalent education and work experience.
* Entry-level position; prior professional experience in financial crimes compliance or investigations is not required. Relevant internship, coursework, or experience in banking, payments, fraud, compliance, investigations, data analysis, or research is preferred.
* No prior AML/BSA, financial crime, transaction monitoring, or investigative experience is required; role-specific knowledge will be provided through training.
* Interest in learning about banking operations, payment services, fintech partnerships, and the broader financial services ecosystem.
* Interest in pursuing a relevant professional certification, such as CAMS or CFE, is a plus but not required.
* Interest in developing knowledge of financial services industry risks, fraud and money laundering typologies, applicable regulations, fintech partnerships, and payment systems.

Community Federal Savings Bank (CFSB) is a federally chartered bank founded in 2001 and headquartered in New York City. We offer a full range of services, including loans, bill payments, card services, internet banking, and merchant processing.

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.

Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. For more than 90 years, Fedcap has been turning possibility into reality. As a global nonprofit serving more than 335,000 people each year across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia, we open doors to economic mobility through innovative, evidence-based solutions in education, workforce development, health, and economic development. **Position Summary**
--------------------

Reporting to the VP of Financial Planning & Analysis, the Labor Cost Analyst plays an important role within our global Finance Planning & Analysis department in analyzing and reporting payroll and workforce-related costs. This position analyzes payroll, fringe benefits, outside labor, and professional fees including allocations to projects/programs. In addition, the Labor Cost Analyst will be responsible for providing detailed payroll and workforce cost analysis on the employee, program, project, and funding-source levels. They will partner with Payroll, HR, HRIS, Finance, Billing, Accounting, and Program Management to ensure payroll data is accurate, allocated appropriately, and effectively incorporated into project budgets, forecasts, financial reporting, and contract billing.

The role goes beyond traditional payroll processing. The successful candidate will analyze how payroll dollars are being utilized across Fedcap’s programs, including salaries, overtime, vacancies, fringe benefits, temporary labor, consultants, and professional services. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, detail-oriented, able to work with large datasets, and experienced in extracting, interpreting payroll and HRIS data.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Payroll Analysis and Reporting**

* Analyze payroll expense by:

  + Employee
  + Program
  + Project
  + Funding Source
  + Grant or Contract
* Analyze actual payroll expense against budget and forecast
* Identify and explain significant payroll variances
* Prepare recurring reports for FP&A, Program Management and Senior Leadership
* Develop and track Payroll Key Performance Indicators (i.e. vacancies, overtime hours, usage of outside labor, payroll as % of revenue)
* Analyze and calibrate payroll allocations

**Project and Workforce Cost Analysis**

* Analyze payroll as a percentage of revenue by project and identify projects with significant changes in labor cost ratios
* Analyze the relationship between staffing levels, vacancies, overtime, outside labor, and project financial performance
* Identify where vacancies or staffing shortages drive increased overtime or outside labor costs
* Perform trend analysis of payroll expense including fringe benefits and identify variance from budget and forecast
* Evaluate whether project staffing and payroll levels are consistent with project revenue, scope, contract requirements and approved budgets
* Provide management with explanations of significant changes to labor to revenue ratios
* Develop analytical models to evaluate the financial impact of staffing changes on project performance

**Cost Allocation and Project Costing**

* Analyze the allocation of administrative and indirect costs across projects
* Understand and evaluate the methodologies for allocation payroll and fringe benefit costs
* Analyze direct allocation of project staff costs and ensure personnel expenses are appropriately assigned to projects and funding sources
* Identify allocation anomalies and work with Finance, Accounting, and Program staff to resolve
* Partner with Billing team to develop a strong understanding of individual project and contract requirements and how it affects billing of allowable project costs which vary under fee for service, cost reimbursement, or fixed price contracts.

**Budgeting and Forecasting**

* Provide detailed financial support of payroll and related costs for annual budget and monthly forecasts
* Support the development of detailed payroll costs assumptions for budget and forecasts including headcount, vacancies, wage changes, merit increases, overtime, turnover, new hires, and external labor
* Develop analyses that assess financial impact of staffing and program changes

**Requirements**
----------------

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in finance or accounting; MBA preferred
* Minimum of 5 years’ related work experience.
* Prior experience with payroll analysis, corporate-level budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and data management.

**Knowledge & Skills**

* Demonstrable knowledge of mission, vision and goals of The Fedcap Group and execution of relevant policies and procedures.
* Strong analytical and communication skills (both verbal and written).
* Payroll analytics and metrics including outside labor and professional fees.
* Support of budgeting for payroll and related costs - For-Profit and Not-For-Profit.
* Experience working with ERP. Knowledge of Oracle Fusion, Smartview, and EPM.
* Strong Microsoft Excel skills and functions (i.e. - Pivot tables, Vlookup, Sumifs)
* Ability to analyze situations accurately, recommend courses of action, and translate complex financial information into clear business insights.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships within FP&A, Accounting, and Program staff.

**Why Join Fedcap**

Join The Fedcap Group and experience The Power of Possible. Be part of a mission-driven organization creating opportunities for individuals facing barriers to economic well-being. Every day, we open doors to economic mobility and stronger communities through education, workforce development

**Procedure and Runbook Development:**

* Establish and maintain IT risk management procedures and any associated runbook in accordance with industry regulations and best practices.
* Ensure software asset management procedures and runbooks are effectively communicated and enforced across the organization.

**Software Asset Management (SAM):**

* Oversee the lifecycle of software assets from acquisition to retirement, ensuring compliance with licensing agreements and optimizing software usage with alignment with Head Office processes.
* Conduct daily health checks and completeness checks for all software assets in the IT Asset Management (ITAM) system.

**Coordination and Collaboration:**

* Coordinate the Annual Recertification processes to ensure ongoing compliance and accuracy of software assets with the IT asset owners.
* Liaise with relevant stakeholders to facilitate IT controls review and reporting, ensuring all controls are met and documented.
* Work closely with internal and external auditors to manage audits including reviewing audit recommendations and timely closure

**ITAM Tool Management:**

* Participate in the tool feature enhancements to improve functionality and ensure it meets organizational needs, especially around SAM area.
* Manage enhancement requests for the tool, working with IT teams to prioritize and implement improvements.

**Monitoring and Reporting:**

* Prepare risk and controls reporting, including controls, Data Risk Strategy (DRS), and operational risk reports for senior management.
* Submit risk acceptances for CIO Office needs, ensuring proper documentation and justification for any exceptions.

**Security and Compliance:**

* Coordinate the implementation and knowledge transfer related to Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for appropriate applications to enhance security measures.
* Oversee ITAM controls operations to ensure adherence to established policies and procedures.

**Training and Awareness:**

* Support implementation of training programs to educate employees on IT risk management practices and software licensing compliance.
* Foster a culture of accountability and awareness around IT risk and asset management within the organization.

**Continuous Improvement:**

* Stay current with industry trends, regulations, and emerging technologies related to IT risk management and software asset management.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance risk management processes and software asset utilization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Science, Risk Management or a related field.
* Minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in IT risk management, IT controls, software asset management, IT asset management or a related area.
* Strong understanding of IT risk frameworks, control processes and software licensing practices.

The salary range for this position will be between $150,000 - $190,000. Natixis is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. Actual base salary will vary and will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, education, skills set, applicable licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. Base salary is only one component of our total rewards package. Natixis also offers a generous benefits package, and you may be eligible for a discretionary incentive award depending on company and individual performance.

jobs.description:
**About FINNY**
===============

FINNY is a growth platform for financial advisors. We are on a mission to make great financial advice easier to find. Today, access to quality financial guidance is limited, not because advisors don't exist, but because the right connections are hard to make when it matters. We're fixing that with AI-powered tools that help advisors find, engage, and retain the clients they can genuinely help.

We've raised a $4.5M Seed from Y-Combinator in S24 and now $17M Series A led by Venrock. We work with over 1,000 firms across the wealth management ecosystem, and have been recognized as the leader in fintech innovation—winning #1 at the Morningstar Fintech Showcase, #1 at 2026 Wealthies, and being featured across the industry.

We're based in Chelsea, NYC, building fast and ambitious systems at the intersection of data, AI, and real-world wealth services.

**About the Team**
==================

You'll join FINNY Engineering and report to our VP of Engineering. The team today is product and backend engineers and a data team. You'll be our first analytics engineer, building the foundation of the company's analytics warehouse on dbt Core and Snowflake.

**About the Role**
==================

FINNY is a metrics-driven company. Until now, our analytics warehouse has been a shared role, divided across several teams. We're bringing it together in a new structure, on a new foundation, and we're hiring a senior Analytics Engineer to own it end to end: the models, the definitions of the metrics the company runs on, and the reports people trust.

You'll work directly with operations, sales, marketing, growth strategy, finance, product and engineering. Success looks like: the metrics the company runs on have tested definitions, a small set of reports is the first place people look, AI tools answer questions about those metrics correctly, and every key business area is covered to the same standard. As the data team grows, you'll help hire and lead it.

**What You’ll Do**
==================

* Own the analytics warehouse day to day: staging and core models, dimensions, facts and identity resolution across our systems
* Define the metrics FINNY runs on, with tests and documentation, so every team works from the same numbers
* Partner with internal stakeholders across the company to turn their questions into models and reports they use
* Own the BI layer: choose the tool and semantic layer, and keep a small set of authoritative reports
* Make the warehouse something AI tools can answer from correctly
* Run the dbt project like software: version control, code review, CI, tests and documentation

**What We’re Looking For**
==========================

* Typically 4+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering or analytics, including owning models that other teams relied on
* Strong SQL and dimensional modeling: facts, dimensions, conformed keys, and a clear grain for every table
* dbt (or an equivalent tool) in production, with git, tests and CI
* You've defined business metrics people used to make decisions, and fixed the cause when two numbers disagreed
* You work directly with non-technical partners and turn vague questions into clear answers—and say "not yet" with a reason
* Scrappy, with ownership: you jump in where help is needed, including work outside your job description
* You're excited to work in person, 5 days a week, in our Chelsea, NYC office

**Nice To Have**
================

* First or early data hire at a startup
* Modeled complex pricing, billing, subscription or usage data
* Made data usable by AI agents: documentation, a semantic layer, guardrails
* Event analytics (PostHog or similar) and CRM data

**Compensation & Benefits**
===========================

FINNY offers a competitive compensation package including:

* Competitive salary and equity
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Flexible paid time off
* 401(k)
* Food and meals provided in our NYC office
* Team offsites and events

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
==============================

FINNY is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to diversity and inclusion in our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Compensation Range: $180K - $210K
